description: Composite figure: four nanoindentation load–depth curve panels (a, c, e, g) plus four dual-axis hardness scatter panels (b, d, f, h). All curve panels share identical axes — Depth (nm), 0–350, and Load (µm), 0–14000, the load unit printed as "µm" (presumably µN). (a) Ni-containing sample, nanosized disk-like B2 in α: four curves legended 500, 700, 900 and 1050 °C, each rising from the origin to a plateau at about the 10000 load gridline and unloading steeply to residual depths between the 100 and 150 nm gridlines. (c) coarse B2 particles in γ of the same sample, same four temperatures, loops clustered closer together and terminating between the 150 and 200 nm gridlines. (e) Ni-free sample, nanosized B2 in α, and (g) Ni-free coarse B2 in γ, each with only two curves (900 and 1050 °C) although the caption says four treatments; the two curves nearly coincide in (g) but separate in (e), where the 900 °C curve lies above the 1050 °C curve during loading. (b), (d), (f), (h) plot hardness (GPa, left axis, error bars) against Annealing Temperature (°C) with a right axis for Ni (wt.%) in (b) and (d) and Al (wt.%) in (f) and (h): hardness of the nanosized B2 in α rises to between the 13 and 14 GPa gridlines in the Ni-containing alloy (b) but falls at 1050 °C in the Ni-free alloy (f), and the coarse B2 in γ of the Ni-free sample (h) contains less Al (~18–19 wt.%) than the nanosized B2 in α (~23–25 wt.%, f).

subfigures.description: Nanoindentation load–depth curves for the Ni-containing sample (nanosized disk-like B2 phase in the α matrix). Axes: Depth (nm) 0–350, Load (µm) 0–14000. Four curves legended 500 °C (red), 700 °C (dark blue), 900 °C (green) and 1050 °C (orange); each rises from the origin to a plateau at about the 10000 load gridline and unloads steeply to a residual depth between the 100 and 150 nm gridlines. The four loops are horizontally offset from one another.

Dual-axis scatter plot: hardness (GPa, left axis 6–16, red squares with error bars) and Ni content (wt.%, right axis, blue squares) versus Annealing Temperature (°C) for the Ni-containing nanosized disk-like B2 in α. Four data points at 500, 700, 900 and 1050 °C. Both series increase monotonically; hardness rises from just above the 10 GPa gridline to between the 13 and 14 GPa gridlines, and the Ni-content series rises from low on the right axis to near its top.

Load–depth curves on the same axes as (a) but for coarse B2 particles precipitated in the γ matrix of the Ni-containing sample; four curves legended 500, 700, 900 and 1050 °C, all reaching the ~10000 load plateau and unloading to residual depths between the 150 and 200 nm gridlines. The loops lie closer together than those in (a).

Dual-axis scatter plot: hardness of the coarse B2 particles in γ of the Ni-containing sample (blue triangles, left axis 6–12 GPa, error bars) and their Ni content (red triangles, right axis, top printed label ~10.2) versus annealing temperature, with four points at 500, 700, 900 and 1050 °C. Hardness rises only modestly, from about the 9.1 GPa level to just above the 10 GPa gridline; the red Ni series also rises monotonically.

Load–depth curves for the Ni-free sample (nanosized disk-like B2 phase in α). Legend contains only two entries, 900 °C (green) and 1050 °C (orange), contrary to the caption's 'four annealing treatments'. The 900 °C curve lies above (higher load at equal depth) the 1050 °C curve during loading; both plateau near the 10000 load gridline and unload to residual depths between the 150 and 200 nm gridlines.

Dual-axis scatter plot: hardness (blue squares, left axis 6–11 GPa, error bars) and Al content (red squares, right axis 22.6–24.8 wt.%) versus annealing temperature for the nanosized B2 in α of the Ni-free sample; only two points, 900 and 1050 °C. Hardness decreases from just below the 9 GPa gridline to between the 8 and 9 GPa gridlines, while Al content increases from about 22.9 to about 24.7 wt.%.

Load–depth curves for coarse B2 particles precipitated in the γ matrix of the Ni-free sample; only two curves, 900 °C (green) and 1050 °C (orange). The two curves nearly coincide over the whole loading branch and plateau at ~10000 load, unloading to residual depths between the 150 and 200 nm gridlines.

Dual-axis scatter plot: hardness (blue triangles, left axis 6–11 GPa, error bars) and Al content (red triangles, right axis 18.2–19.2 wt.%) versus annealing temperature for the coarse B2 in γ of the Ni-free sample, with two points at 900 and 1050 °C. Hardness falls only slightly (about 9.2 to about 9.0 GPa) while Al content increases from about 18.3 to about 19.1 wt.%.

observations.observation: The group is composite: four load–depth nanoindentation curve panels (a, c, e, g) and four dual-axis hardness-versus-annealing-temperature scatter panels (b, d, f, h).
All four curve panels use identical axes labelled 'Depth (nm)' (0 to 350) and 'Load (µm)' (0 to 14000); the load unit is printed as µm (presumably µN).
The legends of (a) and (c) list four annealing treatments — 500 °C, 700 °C, 900 °C and 1050 °C — whereas the legends of (e) and (g) list only 900 °C and 1050 °C.

The caption states that (e) gives load-depth curves for the Ni-free sample 'for the four annealing treatments', but only two curves (900 and 1050 °C) are plotted and legended in that panel; caption and image disagree.

Every curve in (a), (c), (e) and (g) rises from the origin to a plateau at approximately the 10000 load gridline and then unloads steeply to a residual depth (between the 100 and 150 nm gridlines in (a); between the 150 and 200 nm gridlines in (c), (e) and (g)).

In (b) (nanosized disk-like B2 in α of the Ni-containing sample) the red hardness markers with error bars rise monotonically with annealing temperature from just above the 10 GPa gridline to between the 13 and 14 GPa gridlines, while the blue Ni-content markers rise in parallel on the right-hand axis.

In (d) (coarse B2 in γ of the Ni-containing sample) the blue hardness markers rise only from about the 9.1 GPa level to just above the 10 GPa gridline, clearly lower than the hardness of the nanosized B2 in α plotted in (b).

In (f) the hardness of the nanosized B2 in α of the Ni-free sample falls from just below the 9 GPa gridline at 900 °C to between the 8 and 9 GPa gridlines at 1050 °C, while the Al content rises from about 22.9 to about 24.7 wt.%.

In (h) the hardness of the coarse B2 in γ of the Ni-free sample falls only slightly (about 9.2 to about 9.0 GPa) while its Al content rises from about 18.3 to about 19.1 wt.%, well below the >22 wt.% Al of the B2 in α shown in (f).
In (g) the 900 °C and 1050 °C load–depth curves nearly overlap, consistent with the small hardness difference (9.2 vs 9.0 GPa) plotted in (h).

The citing text states that the hardness of the coarse NiAl-type B2 particles precipitated in the γ phase of the Ni-containing sample is less than that of the corresponding precipitates in the α (Fig. 5d).

The citing text states that hardness values increase from 9.1 GPa (Ni: 8.2 wt.%) at 500 °C to 10.5 GPa (Ni: 10.1 wt.%) at 1050 °C; the printed tick labels of the right-hand Ni (wt.%) axis in (d) are only partially legible, so the 8.2 and 10.1 wt.% values cannot be verified from the image.

The citing text states that for the Ni-free sample the coarse FeAl-type B2 particles in γ and the nano-sized B2 particles did not differ significantly: 9.2 GPa at 900 °C (8.9 GPa for nanosized B2 in α) and 9 GPa at 1050 °C (8.3 GPa for the same phase in α).

The citing text states that the Al content of B2 particles formed in the γ phase is less than that of those formed in α (Al being an α stabiliser); the plotted Al axes agree in trend, coarse B2 in γ ~18–19 wt.% (h) vs nanosized B2 in α ~23–25 wt.% (f).
